example.target: Busco la parada de taxis.
example.native: I am looking for the taxi rank.

example.target: Pregunto a una empleada.
example.native: I ask an employee.

example.target: Reviso la placa del taxi.
example.native: I check the taxi's license plate.

example.target: Salgo de la terminal.
example.native: I leave the terminal.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: salgo.

passage.title: La parada oficial del aeropuerto
target: Salgo de la terminal con mi equipaje.
Un hombre dice: Taxi, taxi, barato.
No veo credencial ni licencia.
Le digo: No, gracias.
Pregunto a una empleada: ¿Dónde está la parada oficial de taxis?
Ella dice: Siga el letrero, está cerca.
En la parada de taxis, reviso la placa del taxi.
Pregunto: ¿Usa taxímetro este taxi?
El conductor dice que sí, y subo.
native: I leave the terminal with my luggage.
A man says: Taxi, taxi, cheap.
I see no badge or license.
I tell him: No, thank you.
I ask an employee: Where is the official taxi rank?
She says: Follow the sign, it is close.
At the taxi rank, I check the taxi's license plate.
I ask: Does this taxi use a meter?
The driver says yes, and I get in.

words.note: An ID badge the driver should show.

words.en: Where is the official taxi rank?
words.es: ¿Dónde está la parada oficial de taxis?

words.en: Does this taxi use a meter?
Excuse me, does this taxi have a license?
words.note: Disculpe is polite, with usted.

words.en: I do not need a taxi now, thank you.
words.note: A calm way to refuse unofficial offers.

words.en: I am looking for the official taxi, please.
words.es: Busco el taxi oficial, por favor.

example.target: El conductor confirma el destino.
example.native: The driver confirms the destination.

example.target: Pregunto el nombre del conductor.
example.native: I ask the driver's name.

example.target: Me llamo Luis.
example.native: My name is Luis.

verbs.note: Literally to call oneself. Use se llama for usted.

example.target: Miro la placa en la aplicación.
example.native: I look at the plate in the app.

verbs.native: to get in; to go up

example.target: Ahora subo al carro.
example.native: Now I get in the car.

verbs.note: Subir al carro means to get in the car.

passage.title: Confirmo mi viaje
target: Mi punto de recogida es la entrada del hotel.
Un carro blanco llega.
Miro la placa en la aplicación.
Pregunto: ¿Cómo se llama usted, por favor?
El conductor dice: Me llamo Luis.
El nombre y la foto son correctos.
Digo: Mi destino es el aeropuerto.
El conductor confirma el destino.
Ahora subo al carro.
native: My pickup point is the hotel entrance.
A white car arrives.
I look at the plate in the app.
I ask: What is your name, please?
The driver says: My name is Luis.
The name and the photo are correct.
I say: My destination is the airport.
The driver confirms the destination.
Now I get in the car.

words.note: People also say app.
Some people say coche or auto; carro is common in Mexico and the US.
Usted is polite and right for a driver you do not know.

words.en: Is the plate the one in the app?
words.es: ¿La placa es la de la aplicación?

words.en: I am waiting at the main entrance.
Sorry, can you repeat the plate?
Are you the driver for my trip?
words.es: ¿Usted es el conductor de mi viaje?

example.target: Voy a esta dirección, por favor.
example.native: I am going to this address, please.

verbs.note: Irregular verb. Use ir a plus a place.

example.target: Digo despacio: Morelos.
example.native: I say slowly: Morelos.

verbs.note: Stem change (e to i). Yo form is irregular: digo.

example.target: Pare en la entrada, por favor.
example.native: Stop at the entrance, please.

verbs.note: To one driver, the polite command is pare.

example.target: Le muestro la dirección en mi teléfono.
example.native: I show you the address on my phone.

verbs.note: Stem change (o to ue), except nosotros.

example.target: Repito la dirección despacio.
example.native: I repeat the address slowly.

verbs.note: Stem change (e to i), except nosotros.

passage.title: La entrada del hotel
target: Subo al taxi con mi maleta.
Voy a esta dirección, por favor.
Es el hotel Sol, calle Morelos, número 45.
El punto de referencia es una iglesia blanca.
La entrada está en la esquina.
Hay un letrero verde en la puerta.
Digo despacio: Morelos.
El conductor pregunta: ¿Es la entrada del lado?
Sí, ¿puede parar en la entrada?
native: I get into the taxi with my suitcase.
I am going to this address, please.
It is the Sol hotel, Morelos street, number 45.
The landmark is a white church.
The entrance is on the corner.
There is a green sign on the door.
I say slowly: Morelos.
The driver asks: Is it the side entrance?
Yes, can you stop at the entrance?

words.note: Drivers also hear cerca de plus a place, like cerca de la iglesia.

words.en: I am going to this address, please.
words.es: Voy a esta dirección, por favor.
words.note: A polite, direct way to start.

words.en: Can you stop at the entrance?
words.note: Puede is the polite usted form for one driver.

words.en: Can you repeat the address, please?
I show you the address on my phone.
words.es: Le muestro la dirección en mi teléfono.

words.en: The entrance is on the corner.
words.es: La entrada está en la esquina.

words.en: It is not the main entrance.

example.target: Uso taxímetro, señora.
example.native: I use a meter, ma'am.

example.target: Ella pregunta si hay un cargo extra.
example.native: She asks if there is an extra charge.

example.target: Yo pago el peaje.
example.native: I pay the toll.

example.target: ¿La tarifa incluye el peaje?
example.native: Does the fare include the toll?

verbs.note: Add y before the ending in most forms (incluyo, incluyes), but not in nosotros.

example.target: ¿Cuánto cuesta el viaje al hotel?
example.native: How much does the trip to the hotel cost?

verbs.note: Stem change o to ue. You mostly use cuesta and cuestan.

passage.title: El precio antes de salir
target: Una viajera está en la parada de taxis del aeropuerto.
Ella le pregunta al conductor: ¿Usa taxímetro o precio fijo?
El conductor responde: Uso taxímetro, señora.
Ella pregunta: ¿Hay algún cargo extra?
Él dice: El peaje es un cargo extra.
Ella pide: ¿Me da un precio aproximado al hotel?
El conductor explica: La tarifa del aeropuerto está en el letrero.
La viajera dice: Está bien, vamos al hotel.
Ella pide un recibo al final del viaje.
native: A traveler is at the taxi rank at the airport.
She asks the driver: Do you use a meter or a fixed price?
The driver answers: I use a meter, ma'am.
She asks: Is there any extra charge?
He says: The toll is an extra charge.
She asks: Can you give me an approximate price to the hotel?
The driver explains: The airport rate is on the sign.
The traveler says: That's fine, let's go to the hotel.
She asks for a receipt at the end of the trip.

words.note: Many people also say "metro" or "taxímetro"; taxímetro is safe everywhere.

words.en: Do you use a meter or a fixed price?
Can you give me an approximate price?
Can you repeat the price, please?
words.note: Useful when you do not understand the number.

example.target: Ella pregunta por la ruta más rápida.
example.native: She asks about the fastest route.

example.target: Prefiero la ruta más fácil.
example.native: I prefer the easiest route.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to ie (except nosotros).

example.target: Quiero ir al centro.
example.native: I want to go downtown.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to ie (except nosotros).

example.target: ¿Cuánto cuesta la cuota?
example.native: How much is the toll?

verbs.note: Stem change: o to ue (except nosotros). Usually used in the él and ellos forms.

passage.title: ¿Cuál ruta es mejor?
target: Una viajera sube a un taxi en el aeropuerto.
Ella dice: Buenas tardes, quiero ir al centro.
Después pregunta: ¿Cuál es la ruta más rápida?
El conductor dice que hay una autopista de cuota.
La viajera pregunta: ¿Cuánto cuesta la cuota?
El conductor dice que la cuota es extra.
Ella pregunta: ¿Hay mucho tráfico en la ruta de la ciudad?
Él contesta que sí, hay un poco de tráfico.
Ella dice: Prefiero la ruta más fácil, por favor.
native: A traveler gets into a taxi at the airport.
She says: Good afternoon, I want to go downtown.
Then she asks: What is the fastest route?
The driver says there is a toll highway.
The traveler asks: How much is the toll?
The driver says the toll is extra.
She asks: Is there a lot of traffic on the city route?
He answers that yes, there is a little traffic.
She says: I prefer the easiest route, please.

words.note: In Mexico, cuota means toll. In some countries people say peaje.
Use conductora for a woman.

words.en: Is there a route with less traffic?
I prefer the easiest route, please.
words.es: Prefiero la ruta más fácil, por favor.

words.en: Can you take the scenic route?
words.note: Puede is the polite usted form.

example.target: Según la aplicación, llegamos en 25 minutos.
example.native: According to the app, we arrive in 25 minutes.

example.target: Mi tren sale en 40 minutos.
example.native: My train leaves in 40 minutes.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: salgo.

example.target: El conductor toma un atajo.
example.native: The driver takes a shortcut.

example.target: Después sigue por la calle principal.
example.native: Then he continues on the main street.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i, and yo form is sigo.

example.target: Ella pide otra ruta más rápida.
example.native: She asks for another, faster route.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i. Use pedir for requests, preguntar for questions.

passage.title: Puedo perder mi tren
target: Una viajera sube a un taxi en la estación y habla con el conductor.
Ella dice: Disculpe, ¿hay mucho tráfico hoy?
El conductor responde: Sí, hay un retraso por una obra en la avenida.
Ella pregunta: ¿A qué hora vamos a llegar, más o menos?
Él mira el GPS y dice: Según la aplicación, llegamos en 25 minutos.
Mi tren sale en 40 minutos, así que ella pide otra ruta más rápida.
Primero el conductor toma un atajo, y después sigue por la calle principal.
Al final ella pregunta: ¿Puede dejarme en la entrada de la estación?
El conductor dice que sí, y ella le da las gracias.
native: A traveler gets into a taxi at the station and talks to the driver.
She says: Excuse me, is there a lot of traffic today?
The driver answers: Yes, there is a delay because of road work on the avenue.
She asks: What time are we going to arrive, more or less?
He looks at the GPS and says: According to the app, we arrive in 25 minutes.
My train leaves in 40 minutes, so she asks for another, faster route.
First the driver takes a shortcut, and then he continues on the main street.
In the end she asks: Can you drop me at the station entrance?
The driver says yes, and she thanks him.

words.note: Also means construction site.

words.en: Is there a lot of traffic today?
What time are we going to arrive?
Can you get there on time?
words.note: Polite form with usted, used for one driver.

example.target: Primero recogemos al pasajero en la esquina.
example.native: First we pick up the passenger at the corner.

verbs.note: Yo form changes g to j: recojo.

example.target: Por favor, pare en la esquina.
example.native: Please stop at the corner.

verbs.note: Polite command to one driver: pare.

example.target: Mi amigo espera en la esquina.
example.native: My friend waits at the corner.

example.target: Después seguimos al aeropuerto.
example.native: Then we continue to the airport.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i; yo form is sigo.

passage.title: Una parada para recoger a un amigo
target: Voy en un taxi al aeropuerto con mi equipaje.
Le pregunto al conductor: ¿Puede hacer una parada corta, por favor?
Le explico: Voy a recoger a un amigo en la esquina.
Le digo: El destino final sigue siendo el aeropuerto.
Después pregunto: ¿Cómo cambia la tarifa con la parada?
El conductor dice que el taxímetro sigue funcionando y que la tarifa depende de la ruta.
Primero recogemos al pasajero, y después seguimos al aeropuerto.
Al final, pido el recibo.
native: I am going to the airport in a taxi with my luggage.
I ask the driver: Can you make a short stop, please?
I explain: I am going to pick up a friend at the corner.
I tell him: The final destination is still the airport.
Then I ask: How does the fare change with the stop?
The driver says that the meter keeps running and that the fare depends on the route.
First we pick up the passenger, and then we continue to the airport.
At the end, I ask for the receipt.

words.en: Can you make a short stop, please?
words.es: ¿Puede hacer una parada corta, por favor?
words.note: Polite request to one driver, so use usted.

words.en: I am going to pick up a friend at the corner.
words.es: Voy a recoger a un amigo en la esquina.

words.en: The final destination is still the airport.
words.es: El destino final sigue siendo el aeropuerto.
words.note: Use this so the driver does not change the destination.

words.en: How does the fare change with the stop?
words.es: ¿Cómo cambia la tarifa con la parada?

words.en: Does the meter keep running during the stop?
words.es: ¿El taxímetro sigue corriendo durante la parada?

words.en: I only need a few minutes, thanks.

example.target: ¿Me puede ayudar con la cajuela?
example.native: Can you help me with the trunk?

verbs.note: Regular verb. Usually used with con: ayudar con la maleta.

example.target: El conductor abre la cajuela.
example.native: The driver opens the trunk.

example.target: Ella revisa el asiento antes de bajar.
example.native: She checks the seat before getting out.

example.target: Yo llevo la mochila conmigo.
example.native: I carry the backpack with me.

example.target: Nosotros no olvidamos las bolsas.
example.native: We don't forget the bags.

verbs.note: Often used as se me olvida (I forget): ¿Se me olvida algo?

passage.title: Las maletas en la cajuela
target: Una viajera llega a la parada de taxis con tres bolsas.
Primero, le dice al conductor: Tengo una maleta grande y una mochila pequeña.
Después pregunta: ¿Me puede ayudar con la cajuela, por favor?
El conductor abre la cajuela y pone la maleta grande adentro.
La viajera dice: Esta maleta es frágil, por favor tenga cuidado.
Ella va a llevar la mochila en el asiento con ella.
Al llegar al hotel, el conductor baja las maletas de la cajuela.
Antes de pagar, ella revisa el asiento y pregunta: ¿Se me olvida algo?
Todo está bien, y ella cierra la puerta del taxi.
native: A traveler arrives at the taxi rank with three bags.
First, she tells the driver: I have one big suitcase and one small backpack.
Then she asks: Can you help me with the trunk, please?
The driver opens the trunk and puts the big suitcase inside.
The traveler says: This suitcase is fragile, please be careful.
She is going to carry the backpack on the seat with her.
When arriving at the hotel, the driver takes the suitcases out of the trunk.
Before paying, she checks the seat and asks: Am I forgetting anything?
Everything is fine, and she closes the taxi door.

words.note: Common in Mexico; in other places people say baúl or maletero.

words.en: I have one big suitcase and one backpack.
words.es: Tengo una maleta grande y una mochila.

words.en: Can you help me with the trunk, please?
words.es: ¿Me puede ayudar con la cajuela, por favor?
words.note: Polite request with usted.
Direct but polite request.

words.en: This suitcase is fragile, be careful.
words.es: Esta maleta es frágil, tenga cuidado.

words.en: Can you repeat that, please? I didn't understand.
Am I forgetting anything in the taxi?
words.es: ¿Se me olvida algo en el taxi?

example.target: ¿Puede esperar en la esquina?
example.native: Can you wait on the corner?

example.target: Yo lo llamo si hay tráfico.
example.native: I will call you if there is traffic.

example.target: ¿Cuánto cuesta la espera?
example.native: How much does the wait cost?

verbs.note: Stem change: o to ue. Mostly used in the third person.

example.target: Regreso en diez minutos.
example.native: I come back in ten minutes.

example.target: Le pido su número de teléfono.
example.native: I ask you for your phone number.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to i.

passage.title: Un taxi que espera
target: Primero, el viajero le dice al conductor: Disculpe, ¿puede esperarme unos minutos?
Voy a entrar a la farmacia por un momento.
Después, pregunta: ¿Cuánto cuesta la espera?
El conductor contesta: El taxímetro sigue corriendo, pero le doy un buen precio.
El viajero dice: Está bien, ¿puede esperar en la esquina, frente a la farmacia?
Antes de bajar, le pide el número de teléfono al conductor.
Así puede llamarlo si hay tráfico o si no lo ve.
Al final, el conductor dice: Aquí estoy, tómese su tiempo.
native: First, the traveler says to the driver: Excuse me, can you wait for me a few minutes?
I am going to go into the pharmacy for a moment.
Then he asks: How much does the waiting cost?
The driver answers: The meter keeps running, but I will give you a good price.
The traveler says: Okay, can you wait on the corner, in front of the pharmacy?
Before getting out, he asks the driver for his phone number.
That way he can call him if there is traffic or if he does not see him.
In the end, the driver says: I will be right here, take your time.

words.note: Also mandado in Mexico; both are common.

words.en: Can you wait for me a few minutes, please?
How much does the wait cost?
I am going to come back in ten minutes.
words.es: Voy a regresar en diez minutos.

words.en: Can you give me your phone number?
Where are you going to wait for me?
words.note: Useful to agree on the exact spot.

words.en: I do not understand, can you repeat, please?

example.target: ¿Vamos al hotel Plaza?
example.native: Are we going to the Plaza hotel?

verbs.note: Irregular verb. Also used for the near future: voy a cambiar.

example.target: Veo que el taxista da vuelta a la izquierda.
example.native: I see that the driver is turning left.

verbs.note: The yo form is irregular: veo.

example.target: El taxista revisa el mapa en su teléfono.
example.native: The driver checks the map on his phone.

example.target: Confirmo la dirección con el taxista.
example.native: I confirm the address with the driver.

example.target: Voy a cambiar la ruta.
example.native: I am going to change the route.

verbs.note: Regular -ar verb.

passage.title: Una vuelta equivocada
target: Voy en un taxi con licencia hacia el hotel Plaza.
Primero, veo que el taxista da vuelta a la izquierda.
Entonces le digo con calma: Perdone, ¿vamos al hotel Plaza?
El taxista contesta: Sí, pero hay mucho tráfico en la avenida.
Yo le explico: El hotel está cerca de la estación de tren.
Después, el taxista revisa el mapa en su teléfono.
Me dice: Tiene razón, voy a cambiar la ruta.
Al final, llegamos bien y pido el recibo.
native: I am riding in a licensed taxi to the Plaza hotel.
First, I see that the driver is turning left.
Then I calmly say to him: Excuse me, are we going to the Plaza hotel?
The driver answers: Yes, but there is a lot of traffic on the avenue.
I explain to him: The hotel is near the train station.
After that, the driver checks the map on his phone.
He tells me: You are right, I am going to change the route.
In the end, we arrive safely and I ask for the receipt.

words.note: Same word for men and women.

words.en: Excuse me, are we going to the Plaza hotel?
words.note: Polite way to check without accusing.

words.en: I want to confirm the address, please.
words.es: Quiero confirmar la dirección, por favor.

words.en: The hotel is near the station.
words.es: El hotel está cerca de la estación.
words.note: Use a landmark to help the driver.

words.en: Can you check the map, please?
I think there is a mistake with the route.
words.es: Creo que hay un error con la ruta.

example.target: Quiero que pare en un lugar seguro.
example.native: I want you to stop in a safe place.

verbs.note: After the phrase meaning I want you to, the driver's verb changes to a special form. Use it when you ask someone to stop.

example.target: Si no baja la velocidad, quiero bajar aquí.
example.native: If you do not slow down, I want to get out here.

verbs.note: The same verb means both slowing down and getting out of a car.

example.target: El taxi se detiene frente a la gasolinera.
example.native: The taxi stops in front of the gas station.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form; stem change e to ie.

example.target: Pido un recibo antes de bajar.
example.native: I ask for a receipt before getting out.

verbs.note: Stem change e to i.

example.target: Le explico que tengo miedo.
example.native: I explain to him that I am scared.

passage.title: Pido bajar en un lugar seguro
target: Voy en un taxi con licencia y el conductor maneja muy rápido.
Hay mucho tráfico y el taxista cambia de carril sin avisar.
Le digo con calma: Por favor, vaya más despacio, porque tengo miedo.
El conductor no me escucha y sigue por la misma ruta.
Entonces le explico: Si no baja la velocidad, quiero que pare en un lugar seguro.
Veo una gasolinera con luz y gente, y le pregunto: ¿Puede detenerse cerca de esa gasolinera?
Antes de bajar, pago la tarifa del taxímetro y pido un recibo.
Después salgo del carro, tomo mi maleta y pido otro viaje.
native: I am riding in a licensed taxi and the driver is going very fast.
There is a lot of traffic and the taxi driver changes lanes without signaling.
I say calmly: Please go slower, because I am scared.
The driver does not listen to me and keeps going along the same route.
Then I explain: If you do not slow down, I want you to stop in a safe place.
I see a gas station with lights and people, and I ask him: Can you stop near that gas station?
Before getting out, I pay the fare on the meter and ask for a receipt.
Then I get out of the car, take my suitcase, and request another ride.

words.note: Polite form with usted.

words.en: Can you stop in a safe place?
I want to get out here, please.
I am scared because of the speed.
Can you stop near that gas station?

example.target: Hablamos un poco del barrio y de su trabajo.
example.native: We talk a little about the neighborhood and his job.

example.target: Él recomienda un mercado cerca del parque.
example.native: He recommends a market near the park.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to ie, except nosotros.

example.target: Yo pregunto qué barrio recomienda para cenar.
example.native: I ask which neighborhood he recommends for dinner.

example.target: Él trabaja el turno de la tarde.
example.native: He works the afternoon shift.

example.target: Él conoce bien esta zona.
example.native: He knows this area well.

verbs.note: Irregular yo form: conozco. Use conocer for places and people.

passage.title: Plática con el taxista
target: Subo al taxi y saludo al taxista con una sonrisa.
Le pregunto: ¿Hay mucho tráfico a esta hora?
Él dice que es la hora pico y que la ruta del centro va lenta.
Como el viaje es largo, hablamos un poco del barrio y de su trabajo.
Me cuenta que maneja el turno de la tarde porque conoce bien esta zona.
Yo pregunto: ¿Qué barrio me recomienda para cenar?
Él recomienda un mercado con comida local cerca del parque.
Cuando me pregunta dónde me quedo, digo: Prefiero no dar mi dirección exacta.
Él dice que está bien, y yo sigo mirando la calle.
native: I get into the taxi and greet the driver with a smile.
I ask him: Is there a lot of traffic at this time?
He says it is rush hour and that the route through downtown is slow.
Since the trip is long, we talk a little about the neighborhood and his job.
He tells me he drives the afternoon shift because he knows this area well.
I ask: Which neighborhood do you recommend for dinner?
He recommends a market with local food near the park.
When he asks me where I am staying, I say: I prefer not to give my exact address.
He says that is fine, and I keep looking at the street.

words.note: Same word for men and women.

words.en: Is there a lot of traffic at this time?
Which neighborhood do you recommend for dinner?
words.note: Use usted with a driver you do not know.

words.en: How long have you been working as a taxi driver?
I prefer not to give my exact address.
words.es: Prefiero no dar mi dirección exacta.
words.note: A polite, firm way to protect your privacy.

words.en: Do you know a good place to eat nearby?
words.es: ¿Conoce un buen lugar para comer cerca?

example.target: Yo pago con tarjeta porque no tengo efectivo.
example.native: I pay by card because I do not have cash.

example.target: Pregunto si el recargo nocturno está incluido.
example.native: I ask whether the night surcharge is included.

example.target: Le doy un billete de 50 dólares.
example.native: I give him a 50-dollar bill.

verbs.note: Irregular in the yo form: doy.

example.target: Cuento el cambio con calma.
example.native: I count the change calmly.

verbs.note: Stem change: o to ue.

example.target: Le pido el recibo al taxista.
example.native: I ask the taxi driver for the receipt.

verbs.note: Stem change: e to i. Use pedir for asking for things, preguntar for asking questions.

passage.title: Pagar la tarifa al llegar
target: Llego al hotel y el taxista me muestra el taxímetro.
Son 24 dólares, pero la pantalla también dice que hay un cargo extra por las maletas.
Le pregunto: ¿Puedo pagar con tarjeta, o prefiere efectivo?
El taxista dice que la terminal de pago funciona con tarjeta y con pago sin contacto.
Como es de noche, le pregunto si el recargo nocturno ya está incluido en la tarifa.
Él me explica que sí, y que el total es 30 dólares según el taxímetro.
Le doy un billete de 50 dólares y le pido: ¿Me puede dar el cambio, por favor?
Cuento el cambio con calma, y después le pido el recibo.
Si algo no está claro, prefiero preguntar antes de bajarme del taxi.
native: I arrive at the hotel and the taxi driver shows me the meter.
It is 24 dollars, but the screen also says there is an extra charge for the suitcases.
I ask him: Can I pay by card, or do you prefer cash?
The taxi driver says the payment terminal works with a card and with contactless payment.
Since it is night, I ask him whether the night surcharge is already included in the fare.
He explains to me that it is, and that the total is 30 dollars according to the meter.
I give him a 50-dollar bill and ask: Can you give me the change, please?
I count the change calmly, and then I ask him for the receipt.
If something is not clear, I prefer to ask before getting out of the taxi.

words.note: In Mexico and the US, many people also say billete for a banknote; in some places, papel moneda is less common.

words.en: Can you give me the change, please?
words.es: ¿Me puede dar el cambio, por favor?

words.en: Is the night surcharge already included?
Can you give me a receipt, please?
Why is there an extra charge for the suitcases?
words.es: ¿Por qué hay un cargo extra por las maletas?

words.note: Use aceptan with a driver or company; use acepta to speak politely to one driver.

passage.title: El recibo al final del viaje
target: Llego al hotel después de un viaje de 25 minutos en taxi.
El taxímetro marca la tarifa y yo preparo el pago.
Le digo al conductor: ¿Me puede dar un recibo, por favor?
Lo necesito porque mi empresa pide un comprobante de los gastos de viaje.
El conductor pregunta si quiero el recibo impreso o por correo electrónico.
Prefiero el recibo impreso, pero también le doy mi correo por si acaso.
Si el servicio es bueno, dejo una propina y digo: Gracias por el viaje tranquilo.
Antes de bajar, le agradezco su ayuda con el equipaje y le deseo un buen día.
native: I arrive at the hotel after a 25-minute taxi ride.
The meter shows the fare and I get the payment ready.
I say to the driver: Can you give me a receipt, please?
I need it because my company asks for proof of travel expenses.
The driver asks whether I want the receipt printed or by email.
I prefer the printed receipt, but I also give him my email just in case.
If the service is good, I leave a tip and say: Thank you for the calm ride.
Before getting out, I thank him for his help with the luggage and wish him a good day.

words.note: Often used for expense reports or reimbursements.

words.en: Can you give me a receipt, please?
words.es: ¿Me puede dar un recibo, por favor?
words.note: Polite form with usted, for one driver.

words.en: Can you send it to me by email?
words.es: ¿Me lo puede mandar por correo electrónico?

words.en: I need a receipt for my company.
words.es: Necesito un recibo para mi empresa.
Quédese con el cambio, por favor.
words.note: A common way to leave a tip in cash.

words.en: Does the receipt include the tip?
Thank you very much for your help with the luggage.
words.es: Muchas gracias por su ayuda con el equipaje.

passage.title: Del aeropuerto al hotel
target: Salgo del aeropuerto y busco la parada de taxis porque quiero un taxi autorizado.
Antes de subir, verifico que el taxi tenga la licencia y el número visibles.
Le digo al conductor: Buenas tardes, voy al Hotel Central, por favor.
Si el taxímetro no está encendido, le pregunto: ¿Puede encender el taxímetro, por favor?
Hay mucho tráfico, así que le pido: ¿Puede tomar otra ruta, si es más rápida?
Mientras manejamos, hablamos un poco del clima y de la ciudad.
Al llegar, pregunto cuánto es la tarifa y pago con tarjeta.
Le pido el recibo, le doy las gracias y bajo con mi equipaje con cuidado.
native: I leave the airport and look for the taxi rank because I want a licensed taxi.
Before getting in, I check that the taxi has the license and the number visible.
I tell the driver: Good afternoon, I'm going to the Hotel Central, please.
If the meter is not on, I ask him: Can you turn on the meter, please?
There is a lot of traffic, so I ask him: Can you take another route, if it is faster?
While we drive, we talk a little about the weather and the city.
When we arrive, I ask how much the fare is and I pay by card.
I ask for the receipt, thank him, and get out carefully with my luggage.

words.note: Also: taxi con licencia.

words.en: I'm going to the Hotel Central, please.
words.es: Voy al Hotel Central, por favor.

words.en: Can you turn on the meter, please?
Can you take another route, please?
How much is the fare to the hotel?
words.es: ¿Cuánto es la tarifa hasta el hotel?

words.en: Could you give me the receipt, please?
words.es: Me da el recibo, por favor.
words.note: Polite and common.
